cases.scenario: Draft, rejected and inactive listings are returned (not hidden) to an anonymous viewer - deliberate shipped behavior
cases.steps: GET /listings/<id> with no Authorization, once for each of draft/rejected/inactive
cases.response_assertions: body.listingStatus equals the fixture's real state (draft/rejected/inactive); full DTO returned (seller block, price, images present)
cases.business_outcome: Only pending_approval is gated from the public; draft/rejected/inactive stay publicly readable - a deliberate, tested, documented product decision (BRI-44), confirmed against listings.service.ts:786,60 and listings.service.spec.ts:965-972. This is the actual shipped behavior the sheet's row title contradicts (CF-038-01); that conflict is tracked separately by TC-038-013/016/023, which assert the sheet's literal (404) claim and stay BLOCKED pending a product decision.
cases.source: Audit Finding #1 (listings.service.ts:786, :60); listings.service.spec.ts:965-972; docs/domain.md:70 (BRI-44); audit suggested scenarios #2-#3

cases.scenario: Draft, rejected and inactive listings are returned to a logged-in non-owner buyer, same as to a guest
cases.preconditions: draft=cmw9clmdw00j0u4pw44r26fdu, rejected=cmw9clw0s00jcu4pwqqaxg3bu, inactive=cmw9clyw100jhu4pwknnq2foc; needs a second logged-in buyer account distinct from the fixtures' owner
cases.steps: GET /listings/<id> with a non-owner buyer's Bearer token, once for each of draft/rejected/inactive
cases.response_assertions: same as anon: full DTO returned, listingStatus unchanged
cases.business_outcome: Confirms OptionalJwtAuthGuard treats a logged-in non-owner identically to a guest for these states (isOwner/isAdmin both false) - Finding #1 / audit suggested scenarios #2-#3, Buyer role.

cases.source: Audit Finding #1; audit suggested scenarios #2-#3 (Buyer role); fixtures.json _owners_readme

cases.scenario: Soft-deleted listing 404s even for its own owner - confirmed shipped behavior
cases.preconditions: soft-deleted listing fixture needed (deletedAt set); owner = the seller who deleted it
cases.test_data: no soft-deleted fixture currently in fixtures.json _states
cases.steps: GET /listings/<soft-deleted-id> with the owner's Bearer token
cases.response_assertions: body.message == 'Listing not found'
cases.business_outcome: Soft-delete (deletedAt) hides a listing from literally everyone including its own owner - the opposite asymmetry from the sheet's 'owner can still see it' framing (Finding #2). Confirmed by listings.repository.ts:692-704 (findFirst with NOT_DELETED, no owner bypass) and docs/domain.md:75.
cases.blocked_reason: no fixture resource in state 'soft_deleted' (no deletedAt listing in fixtures.json _states)
cases.source: Audit Finding #2; listings.repository.ts:692-704; docs/domain.md:75; audit suggested scenario #7

cases.scenario: A listing demoted back to pending_approval still 404s for a non-owner even if its DTO is cached from when it was live
cases.preconditions: requires a listing to transition from a live/public state back to pending_approval between two reads of the same cached DTO (listing:<id>); no documented endpoint performs a live-to-pending_approval transition
cases.steps: GET listing (caches DTO while live) -> trigger a live-to-pending_approval transition -> GET the same id again, expect 404 despite the cached DTO
cases.response_assertions: second GET returns 404 even though the first GET's DTO is still cached under listing:<id>
cases.business_outcome: Confirms the shared listing:<id> cache is re-gated on every request, not just at population time (listings.service.ts:780-788) - already proven at unit level (listings.service.spec.ts:999-1007); this is the integration-level counterpart, audit suggested scenario #12.
cases.blocked_reason: no endpoint/fixture available to move a listing from a live state back to pending_approval, and no cache-manipulation hook in this harness; needs backend/QA confirmation this transition is reachable via the app before an E2E sequence can be scripted

cases.scenario: OpenAPI spec declares no auth/security requirement for GET /listings/:id despite the code enforcing optional-auth-based visibility
cases.preconditions: Inspect schemathesis/spec/openapi.pretty.json operationId ListingsController_findById and the whole spec file
cases.steps: Static spec review: grep the operation object and the whole spec file for a 'security' field
cases.response_assertions: spec declares a security/auth requirement for this operation
cases.business_outcome: The spec documents no auth requirement at all (0 'security' occurrences repo-wide) while the code enforces optional-auth-based visibility (OptionalJwtAuthGuard + owner/admin bypass) - a spec-gap, not a code bug. Completes Finding #9 / CF-038-03 alongside TC-038-051 (functional proof of guard behavior).
cases.source: audit Finding #9; Source agreement matrix row 'Auth requirement on this route'; CF-038-03; schemathesis/spec/openapi.pretty.json
